questions.text:
For any two languages L1 and L2 such that L1 is context-free and L2 is recursively enumerable but not recursive, which of the following is/are necessarily true?
I. [latex]\bar{L_{1}}[/latex] (complement of L1) is recursive
II. [latex] \bar{L_{2}}[/latex] (complement of L2) is recursive
III. [latex]\bar{L_{1}}[/latex] is context-free
IV. [latex]\bar{L_{1}} \cup L_{2}[/latex] is recursively enumerable
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: CFLs are decidable, and recursive languages are closed under complement [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: if [latex]\bar L_2[/latex] were recursive, L2 would be recursive [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- III: CFLs are not closed under complement [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not necessarily
- IV: [latex]\bar L_1[/latex] is recursive (so RE), and RE is closed under union [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True

Answer: I and IV only

questions.text:
Consider the following Deterministic Finite Automaton M.


Let S denote the set of eight bit strings whose second, third, sixth and seventh bits are 1. The number of strings in S that are accepted by M is
questions.solution:
Strings look like [latex]b_1\,1\,1\,b_4\,b_5\,1\,1\,b_8[/latex] (16 strings). To accept, the DFA must reach the 4th state (via "0" from state 3) and then read a 1.

Tracing all cases, this happens only for [latex]b_1=0, b_4=1, b_5=0[/latex]:
0 1 1 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] state 3, then 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] state 4, then 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] accept. [latex]b_8[/latex] can be 0 or 1.

Accepted strings: 01110110, 01110111 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2

Answer: 2

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE with respect to possible outcomes of executing a Turing Machine over a given input?
questions.solution:
On any input, a TM can only halt and accept, halt and reject, or run forever. "Halt by changing the input" is not an outcome (writing on the tape is just part of computing).

Answer: it may halt by changing the input

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: it may halt and accept the input
it may halt by changing the input
it may halt and reject the input

questions.text: The following Finite Automaton recognizes which of the given languages?
questions.solution:
Transitions: A on 1 stays, A on 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B; B on 0 stays, B on 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] C (final); C on 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B, C on 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] A.

We reach C exactly when the last two symbols are 0 then 1, so it accepts strings ending in 01.

Answer: [latex]\{1,0\}^*\{01\}[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: How many states are there in a minimum state deterministic finite automaton accepting the language [latex]L=\left\{w \mid w \in\{0,1\}^{*}\right.[/latex], number of 0's is divisible by 2 and number of 1's is divisible by 5, respectively }?
questions.solution:
Track (number of 0s mod 2, number of 1s mod 5). All 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 combinations are distinguishable, so the minimal DFA has 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 10 states.

Answer: 10
